title: Unmasking the robots: Why it’s critical to discover AI agent identities and how Tenable helps you secure them
summary: Explore Microsoft Entra Agent ID and AI identity security best practices, & include identities in your unified asset inventory.
body_markdown:
Discover how to secure AI agents in your cloud environment with Tenable One Cloud Exposure. We explore Microsoft Entra Agent ID and provide essential best practices for robust agentic AI identity security.


## Key takeaways


1. Understand your current maturity level and then build an appropriate action plan to secure your agent identities.
2. Use your cloud providers’ native tools or Tenable One Cloud Exposure to locate and catalog every AI agent operating in your environment.
3. Do not assign human identities or over-privileged service accounts to the AI agents your vendors deploy in your environment. Instead, require that vendors adopt official models like Microsoft Entra Agent ID for their AI agents’ identities.


As[AI agents](https://www.tenable.com/cyberagents-exchange) move from experimental toys to tools that make autonomous decisions, interact with databases, and call external APIs, organizations need to be clear on who — or what — is executing these actions in their cloud environments.


## Why non-human identities (NHIs) aren’t secure enough for AI agents


Security teams categorize identities into two buckets: human identities and[non-human identities](https://www.tenable.com/blog/secure-ai-attack-surface-exposure-management#:~:text=non%2Dhuman%20identities) (NHIs), such as service accounts, secrets, and automated scripts.


Treating AI agents as standard NHIs is a recipe for disaster. AI agents combine their non-deterministic nature with their ability to execute flexible, outcome-oriented actions, rather than following strict, prescribed instructions.


Unlike classic, predictable scripts that follow rigid code paths, AI agents:


- Make creative, runtime decisions using LLMs.
- Interact with dynamic external tools, memory caches, and knowledge bases.
- Constantly adapt to solve problems, making it difficult for a security team to establish AI agents’ baseline behavior.


To address this challenge, major cloud providers have introduced dedicated, specialized agentic AI identity models. Let’s break down one major model: Microsoft Entra Agent ID.


### Microsoft Entra Agent ID


**Feature / dimension** **Microsoft Entra Agent ID**


**Primary architecture** Identity provider-centric (built on Entra ID)


**Target scope** Any AI platform, including Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and third-party platforms not hosted on Azure


**Identity components** Four-object model: Agent identity blueprint, agent identity blueprint principal, agent identity, agent user


**Hardening mechanism** Permission boundaries and cascade rules; “On-behalf-of” user plus agent dual authentication


**Developer complexity** Higher, due to dealing with a multi-object model, with cross-tenant considerations


**Visibility / scope** Excellent, since it covers unmanaged and external SaaS-based agents


## Announcing Tenable One Cloud Exposure support for Microsoft Entra Agent ID


Identity and cloud providers' native identity management tools present only basic information about agentic identities, without providing context about their security flaws and how they extend your attack surface. Because AI agents are becoming a new class of[identity](https://www.tenable.com/blog/identity-is-the-new-battleground-why-proactive-security-is-the-way-forward) with real permissions, you must understand how an attacker could compromise and abuse them. At Tenable, we believe visibility is the foundation of security. You can’t secure assets that you do not know exist.


As organization-wide adoption of[agentic AI](https://www.tenable.com/blog/agentic-ai-security-keep-your-cyber-hygiene-failures-from-becoming-a-global-breach) accelerates, the immediate challenge for security teams is first and foremost finding them. Because these identities are brand new, conventional[identity and access management](https://www.tenable.com/blog/identity-is-the-new-battleground-why-proactive-security-is-the-way-forward#:~:text=IAM) (IAM) systems may not recognize or monitor them, which creates security blind spots.


To help our customers address this issue,[Tenable One Cloud Exposure](https://www.tenable.com/cloud-security/products/cnapp) **now brings Microsoft Entra agentic AI identities directly into your unified asset and identity inventory.**


### Microsoft Entra Agent ID Model


The Microsoft Entra Agent ID framework functions through a four-tiered structural model:


1. **Agent identity blueprints** serve as the master templates for shared attributes. Residing exclusively within the agent provider’s home tenant, they establish cross-tenant links that heighten exposure to potential supply-chain attacks.
2. **Agent identity blueprint principals** are the localized instantiation of a blueprint within every specific tenant where the AI agent is deployed and active.
3. **Agent identities** represent the functional identities utilized for routine tasks. To maintain oversight of agent behavior, these are the primary entities your security team must monitor.
4. **Agent users** offer an optional layer for each agent identity requiring human-centric features — like Microsoft Teams access or a personal mailbox — to function effectively as integrated “digital colleagues.”
